testemunhos.goncalo: I contacted Globalead looking for car insurance options and was helped by Carlos Gonçalves. From the very first conversation he was extremely professional and helpful. He laid out the best options for what I needed, talked me through each proposal in detail, and handled the whole process very efficiently. My policy was active in under 24 hours. I was delighted with the service and thoroughly recommend Globalead for how quick, clear and professional they were.
testemunhos.francisco: When Carlos first got in touch on behalf of Globalead Portugal, the confidence and commitment came across immediately. He promised thorough, dedicated work on the sale of my property, and he kept every word of it. Throughout the process Carlos was tireless — always available, always helpful, attentive to every detail. He helped me gather all the paperwork and guided me step by step, turning what could have been a difficult process into a calm and secure one. The result was far more than a completed sale: it was knowing I can count on someone who puts professionalism and humanity side by side. I am deeply grateful for his work and certain that Carlos will always be my first choice.
testemunhos.familiaGomes: We got in touch with Globalead after seeing an advert on social media, at a point when we were looking for help with a mortgage application. With their support we ended up with a monthly payment that was fair, comfortable and genuinely suited to our family budget. On top of that, they helped us renegotiate our home and life insurance. Special thanks to Carlos, who was beside us throughout with professionalism, dedication and enormous availability. He made the whole process simple and calm, and left us certain we can count on him again.
testemunhos.liliana: Thank you Carlos for all the help, dedication and professionalism in getting this deal done. Throughout the process you were transparent, responsible and ethical, explaining everything clearly. You listened to my concerns and respected my pace. I recommend you without hesitation and believe we will work together again. Wishing you every success!
testemunhos.wneres: Thank you for all your help over these months, Carlos. You were a true professional. After so much persistence, paperwork and bureaucracy, we have finally bought our first home in Portugal. You were tireless throughout, from the mortgage support to completing the purchase, staying close to us from the start right through to the deed. We are very grateful we found you and for all the dedication you showed along the way.
testemunhos.ana: I want to highlight the commitment shown throughout the process, and especially how clearly and openly every question was answered. The breadth of services brought in to support the sale also made a real difference and, in my view, contributed significantly to how well the deal went. Thank you for all the professionalism and dedication.

sobre.heroTexto: Our story, our values, and the standard we hold ourselves to
sobre.p1: Globalead stands out for its integrated, forward-looking approach, working as an intermediary to build tailored solutions that make every process comfortable, secure and efficient. Founded to fill a gap in the market, the company pioneered managing and supporting clients across multiple areas at once, with each client’s needs at the centre of how it operates.
sobre.p2: Globalead specialises in the property market, supported by services in insurance, lending, alarm systems, telecoms and energy. The company combines a modern approach with long-established experience, and has become a reference point in its sector.
sobre.p3: The team is made up of highly qualified, committed professionals who offer a personal service built on innovation, creativity and anticipating what clients will need. Globalead simplifies the client experience, providing free, centralised support from the first conversation through to completion.
sobre.p4: Present at every stage of the client journey, Globalead raises the experience to a new level of convenience and satisfaction, earning recommendations and reinforcing its reputation as a network of outstanding intermediation and management.
sobre.razao1Texto: We give you access to advanced, reliable and effective solutions, tailored to what you actually need.
sobre.razao2Texto: We analyse your requirements and recommend the right solution, always with the quality and guarantees of the brands we represent.
sobre.razao3Texto: Choosing Globalead means a personal service with access to the best the market has to offer.
sobre.razao4Texto: We represent the quality, innovation and reliability of our partners, so that the support you get is the best available.

sobre.objetivo1: Offer tailored, integrated solutions adapted to each client’s specific needs, with a focus on the property sector.
sobre.objetivo2: Act as an intermediary, comparing mortgages, telecoms, energy and insurance to put the best options in front of clients.
sobre.objetivo3: Simplify and streamline processes, with support that is personal, responsive, straightforward and free.
sobre.objetivo4: Deliver comfort, security and efficiency through rigorous management, backed by a specialist team committed to the best outcome for each client.
sobre.objetivo5: Build lasting relationships of trust, earning client loyalty through service quality, closeness and transparency at every stage.
sobre.objetivo6: Support the client at every stage, from first contact to completion, through a single point of contact that keeps the experience simple.

certificacao.heroTitulo: We take care of your energy certificate
certificacao.p1: At Globalead Portugal we understand that selling or letting a property can be a complex process, full of details that need attention. One indispensable step — both for legal compliance and for the value of your property — is obtaining the energy certificate.
certificacao.p2: The energy certificate is an official document assessing a property’s energy efficiency. It states the energy rating (A+ to F) and sets out recommended improvements with estimated savings. It is issued by experts qualified by ADENE under the Portuguese Building Certification System (SCE) and governed by Decree-Law no. 101-D/2020.
certificacao.p3: We support you from the start of the process through to the certificate being issued — quickly, simply and without worry. Lean on our experience and concentrate on what actually matters: closing the deal.
certificacao.agendamentoTexto: Once you get in touch we call you within 24 hours to book the surveyor’s visit.
certificacao.documentacaoTexto: The necessary paperwork needs to be gathered before the visit.
certificacao.visitaTexto: A qualified surveyor collects everything needed on site.
certificacao.emissaoTexto: We deliver your certificate 48 to 72 hours after the visit.
certificacao.apartamentosTexto: We assess energy use in residential apartments, report on efficiency and identify where improvements can be made.
certificacao.moradiasTexto: We carry out detailed energy assessments of detached and semi-detached homes, helping owners understand and improve their property’s efficiency.
certificacao.comercioTexto: For retail and service premises we report on the building’s energy performance and suggest measures to cut energy costs and improve sustainability.

imoveis.question: How do I sell my property with Globalead?
imoveis.answer: Get in touch for a free valuation. We handle the whole process — marketing, viewings and negotiation — right through to the deed.

imoveis.question: How long does it take to sell a property?
imoveis.answer: It depends on the type of property and its location, but on average we sell within 30 to 90 days.

imoveis.question: What documents do I need to sell my property?

seguros.question: What is insurance?
seguros.answer: Insurance is an agreement between an insurer and a policyholder, under which the insurer takes on specific cover in the event of a claim and pays out according to the sum insured. The policyholder pays the premium, and the contract is set out in the policy document, which defines both the cover and the cost. The payout may go to the policyholder, to a named beneficiary, or to a third party who suffered loss attributable to the policyholder.

seguros.question: What is an insurance policy?
seguros.answer: The policy is the contract between the insurer and the policyholder, and it contains the general, particular and special conditions of the cover. The general conditions are standard clauses applied to similar risks, while the particular and special conditions are adjusted to the type of insurance and the specific needs of the person insured.

seguros.question: How does car insurance work?
seguros.answer: Car insurance is a contract between the policyholder and the insurer that transfers responsibility for damage caused by the use of a vehicle. Third-party liability cover is required by law and covers damage to others only. To protect your own vehicle you need own-damage cover (fully comprehensive). The premium is influenced by your age, driving experience and claims history, the vehicle’s characteristics and how it is used, where it is parked, annual mileage, safety equipment, and other factors relating to both driver and vehicle.

seguros.question: What types of insurance are there?
seguros.answer: The market offers a wide range, including around 200 policies made compulsory by law for particular professions. They fall into categories such as: workplace accidents, accidents on duty, personal accident, personal assistance, damage, illness, fire, surety, civil liability, theft and life.

seguros.question: What is third-party liability insurance?
seguros.answer: Third-party liability cover is required by law and protects passengers and third parties in the event of an accident, covering both injury and material damage. The minimum cover set by the ASF is €1,220,000 for material damage and €6,070,000 for bodily injury, reviewed every five years. It does not cover injuries to the driver responsible for the accident, damage to their own vehicle, or damage from accidents caused deliberately or through negligence of road safety rules.

seguros.question: Is life insurance important?
seguros.answer: Life insurance covers the risk of death or, alternatively, of survival. On death, the insurer pays an agreed sum to the beneficiaries; on survival, it pays a sum to the insured person at the end of the contract. Mixed policies combine both, and cover can be extended with additions such as disability or unemployment. It provides financial security for the family, particularly where income is lost or where longevity increases costs.

seguros.question: Am I required to take life insurance with a mortgage?
seguros.answer: If a bank requires life insurance when you take out a mortgage, that requirement is not imposed by law. Under Decree-Law no. 222/2009 the bank must inform you that life insurance is available, but you are free to choose which company you buy it from.

seguros.question: What is home multi-risk insurance for?
seguros.answer: Home multi-risk insurance provides compensation for damage to the property and its contents from events such as natural disasters, fire, explosion, theft, water damage and electrical faults, among others. It goes well beyond the cover required by law, which only covers fire damage to buildings held in horizontal property (commonhold), giving the home much broader protection.

certificacao.question: What is an energy certificate?
certificacao.answer: The energy certificate is a document rating a property’s energy efficiency on a scale from A+ (very efficient) to F (inefficient). It is issued by experts authorised by ADENE, the Portuguese energy agency. It sets out the property’s energy consumption for heating, cooling and hot water, along with recommended improvements to reduce it.

certificacao.question: What is an energy certificate for?
certificacao.answer: Since 2013 an energy certificate has been compulsory for anyone selling or letting a property. Its purpose is to tell the owner how the property performs and what improvements could be made.

certificacao.question: What are the benefits of energy certification?
certificacao.answer: For owners selling or letting, certification brings real advantages. It can increase the property’s value and, by pointing to the right energy measures, reduce consumption and therefore cost. Certification can also open the door to tax benefits: a property rated A or above may qualify for a reduction of up to 25% in IMI (municipal property tax).

certificacao.question: What documents are needed for the survey?
certificacao.answer: The compulsory documents are the Caderneta Predial Urbana (urban property record) and the Certidão de Registo Permanente (permanent registry certificate). You may also provide optional documents such as the building’s technical data sheet, the floor plan and the construction cross-section, which help achieve the best possible rating for your property.

certificacao.question: Who can issue an energy certificate?
certificacao.answer: Only an expert qualified by ADENE may produce an energy certificate. These are architects or engineers with at least five years’ experience, working under the Portuguese Building Energy Certification System (SCE), established by Decree-Law no. 101-D/2020 of 7 December.

certificacao.question: How long is an energy certificate valid?
certificacao.answer: It is valid for 10 years for residential buildings and small commercial or service premises. For large commercial and service buildings the term is 6 years for certificates issued up to 30 April 2015, and 8 years for those issued after that date.

certificacao.question: Can I use the energy certificate for the deed?
certificacao.answer: Energy certificates can be used for the purposes of the deed only when accompanied by a permanent registry certificate that is valid for that purpose.

certificacao.question: When is an energy certificate compulsory?
certificacao.answer: Article 18 of Decree-Law no. 101-D/2020 makes the certificate compulsory when: letting, selling, transferring a business lease, or transferring property in lieu of payment; constructing new buildings; carrying out major renovations costing more than 25% of the property’s value; operating large commercial or service buildings (over 1,000 m², or 500 m² for certain uses), which are subject to periodic inspection; and applying to programmes that require the certificate for funding or tax benefits.

certificacao.question: Do commercial premises legally need an energy certificate?
certificacao.answer: Yes. Decree-Law 101-D/2020 applies to all buildings intended for human occupation, commercial premises included. If the premises are sold, transferred or let for more than four months, a certificate must be issued. For premises over 250 m², an initial assessment is carried out first, followed by a quotation for producing the certificate.

certificacao.question: What are the fines for selling or letting without a certificate?
certificacao.answer: Advertising, selling or letting a property without first obtaining the energy certificate is an administrative offence, punishable by a fine of up to €3,750 for individuals and up to €44,890 for companies, under article 35 of Decree-Law 101-D/2020.

credito.question: How much can I borrow?
credito.answer: Before you start looking at properties, work out how much you can borrow based on your savings and monthly income. Set aside 15% to 20% of the purchase price as a deposit — the bank will not lend the full value, and there are taxes and extra costs on top. Ideally, the monthly payment should not exceed 35% of your net monthly income.

credito.question: Why talk to a credit intermediary?
credito.answer: You get personal guidance without having to visit every bank yourself, a single consolidated comparison of the offers currently available, a simpler application process, and often better terms than you would get alone.

credito.question: Sending the documents needed for a mortgage application
credito.answer: Banks can only make you a personalised offer once you have sent documents evidencing your financial position. Without them, the offers are generic and tell you little about what you would actually get. A personalised proposal sets out the interest rate, the spread, the fees and the cost of any additional products required. Going through each component in detail is what reveals where there is room to negotiate. Globalead Portugal guides you through it so the decision is an informed one.

credito.question: Receiving mortgage offers and comparing them
credito.answer: Banks can only make you a personalised offer once you have sent documents evidencing your financial position. Without them, the offers are generic and tell you little about what you would actually get. A personalised proposal sets out the interest rate, the spread, the fees and the cost of any additional products required. Going through each component in detail is what reveals where there is room to negotiate. Globalead Portugal guides you through it so the decision is an informed one.

credito.question: Requesting the property valuation
credito.answer: Banks require an official valuation of the property as part of the mortgage process. It establishes the property’s real value and lets the lender assess the risk. The valuation costs between €200 and €350 depending on the bank. Globalead Portugal follows the whole procedure, keeping it transparent and on schedule.

credito.question: The binding mortgage offer: the FINE
credito.answer: The FINE is issued once the valuation and any further checks are complete, assuming the mortgage is approved. It sets out the loan amount, how the funds will be released, the interest rate, the repayment schedule, the fees and any other costs. You have 30 days to review it and decide whether to accept. Before the deed, it is essential to go through every condition and clear up any doubts. Globalead Portugal has specialists on hand for this decisive stage.

credito.question: Signing the mortgage and completing the purchase deed
credito.answer: When you accept the mortgage offer, the bank issues the FINE (European Standardised Information Sheet), detailing the amount, interest rate, fees, repayment schedule and other charges. After the FINE is delivered there is a minimum period of 7 days before the deed, so you can reflect and confirm the decision matches what was agreed. That interval exists to make sure you fully understand every contractual term. Globalead Portugal recommends asking for detailed information and resolving every question before signing anything.

credito.question: What is the spread?
credito.answer: The spread is the part of the interest rate that each bank sets individually on a mortgage — essentially the lender’s profit margin. The spread you are offered depends largely on your risk profile (credit history, income, the amount you are borrowing, the guarantees you can provide) and, frequently, on which additional products you agree to take in order to bring it down.

credito.question: What is the difference between a fixed and a variable rate?
credito.answer: A fixed rate stays the same for the life of the loan and is agreed with the lender when you apply. A variable rate moves with an index, so it changes over the life of the loan and your monthly payment changes with it: if the index rises, so does your rate; if it falls, your rate falls too. In Portugal the index normally used for mortgages is Euribor, at 3, 6 or 12 months.

credito.question: What is the Nominal Annual Rate (TAN)?
credito.answer: The Nominal Annual Rate (TAN) applies to all operations involving interest, whether investments or loans, and lets you compare products against each other. On a variable-rate mortgage it is simply the spread added to Euribor.

credito.question: What is Euribor?
credito.answer: Euribor — the Euro Interbank Offered Rate — is the interest banks pay other institutions to fund their activity. It is calculated as the average of the rates offered by the 52 largest banks in the euro area over a given term. Euribor is not fixed and moves daily, but you choose the point at which your rate is recalculated. The most common terms are 3, 6 and 12 months.

credito.question: How do I get a mortgage approved?
credito.answer: To get approval quickly, give the lender as many guarantees as you can, so it perceives less risk. Beyond your income level, a good record of repaying previous loans is essential, and banks place a lot of weight on job stability. Ideally the monthly payment should not exceed 40% of the household’s income.

credito.question: Which banks offer the 100% public guarantee?
credito.answer: Every bank that grants mortgages in Portugal — 17 institutions in total — has signed up to the public guarantee, including all the partners we already work with.

credito.question: What is the deadline to apply for the guarantee?
credito.answer: To benefit from the public guarantee and 100% financing, the credit agreement must be signed by 31 December 2026.

credito.question: Are there fees if I miss a mortgage payment?
credito.answer: If you do not pay on the due date you are in arrears, and the bank may charge default interest and a debt recovery fee. Default interest is a surcharge of up to 3% a year on top of the ordinary interest rate. The debt recovery fee cannot exceed 4% of the instalment, subject to a minimum of €12 and a maximum of €150.

credito.question: What happens if I default on my mortgage?
credito.answer: Defaulting on a mortgage is a situation no borrower wants. The first time you miss a payment, the bank has 15 days to contact you. Between the 31st and 60th day after the default, the case enters PERSI (the out-of-court procedure for regularising defaults), which exists to reach an agreement between the bank and the customer.

credito.question: Can I still get a tax exemption?
credito.answer: Yes. You may still benefit from exemption from IMT (property transfer tax) and Stamp Duty, which generate significant savings when buying a home.

credito.question: How long does the state guarantee last?
credito.answer: The guarantee remains in force for ten years from the date of the mortgage deed.

credito.question: Is the instalment processing fee still charged?
credito.answer: The processing fee is charged on each instalment paid (plus Stamp Duty) for the whole life of the loan, applied monthly when the payment is taken. Although the processing fee was abolished in January 2021, that only applies to new loans.

credito.question: Early repayment: what are my rights and the costs?
credito.answer: You have the right to repay your loan early, in full or in part, before the scheduled date. Early repayment does carry a cost: on a variable rate the fee cannot exceed 0.5% of the capital repaid; on a fixed rate it cannot exceed 2%.

credito.question: Can my mortgage spread change?
credito.answer: It is uncommon, but the spread can change during the life of the contract. This can happen where you agreed with the bank to meet certain conditions in exchange for a lower spread — such as having your salary paid into an account with them, or keeping direct debits active on it — and then stop meeting those conditions.

credito.question: What is the Annual Percentage Rate of Charge (TAEG)?
credito.answer: The Annual Percentage Rate of Charge (TAEG) represents the total cost of the mortgage, including every charge attached to the contract: interest, fees, taxes, insurance linked to the loan, and the cost of maintaining the current account tied to it. It also covers other costs such as the fees charged for registering the mortgage.

politicaPrivacidade.texto: Privacy Policy
Information on the processing of personal data
At Globalead Portugal, the privacy and protection of the personal data of our clients and of all other data subjects is a priority.
This Privacy Policy describes how we process personal data, who we share it with, how long we keep it, and how the data subject can contact the controller to exercise their rights.
Accessing and using the Globalead Portugal website, and subscribing to the services offered through it, means the user accepts and is bound by this Privacy and Data Protection Policy.
Data Controller
Globalead Portugal, as the controller of the personal data of its Users and Clients, determines the purposes and means of processing that data.
Any question relating to the processing of personal data should be addressed to: geral@globalead.pt
Lawfulness of Processing, Purposes and Legal Basis
For the purposes of this Policy, personal data means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person.
Globalead Portugal undertakes to process personal data lawfully, fairly and transparently, collecting only the data strictly necessary to provide estate agency services, namely to:

itens: Produce statistics on how the website is used
Improve and develop the website
Provide estate agency services
Respond to requests for contact, information or clarification
Send newsletters, where subscribed to
Present business opportunities suited to the User's profile
Analyse aggregated data in order to manage and improve the business
Perform contracts or take steps prior to entering into a contract
Comply with legal and tax obligations
Situations in which the data subject has given prior, express consent

politicaPrivacidade.texto: Personal Data Collected

itens: Name, telephone number and email address
Data provided through the forms available on the website
Preferences, interests and commercial information
Civil and tax identification data required to enter into contracts
Where applicable, information about assets, in the case of selling clients

politicaPrivacidade.texto: Personal data may be collected through the website, by email, by telephone, in person, or during property viewings carried out as part of our estate agency activity.
Consent
By submitting personal data through the website, the User declares that they have read, understood and accepted this Privacy Policy, and authorises the corresponding processing.

By entering into an estate agency contract, or by voluntarily requesting information about properties, the User consents to Globalead Portugal processing their personal data for the purposes of communication, marketing and presenting business opportunities suited to their profile. That consent may be withdrawn at any time.
Collection, Use and Recipients of the Data

itens: The personal data provided forms part of the Globalead Portugal database
The data may be used for commercial communication and direct or indirect marketing
The data is processed by electronic means
Access to the data is restricted to authorised staff or service providers

politicaPrivacidade.texto: The User may at any time ask for their personal data to stop being used for marketing purposes, by writing to geral@globalead.pt.
Data Subject's Rights

itens: Right of access
Right to rectification
Right to erasure
Right to restriction of processing
Right to data portability
Right to object
Right to withdraw consent

politicaPrivacidade.texto: These rights may be exercised by email to geral@globalead.pt.
Complaints
The data subject has the right to lodge a complaint with the Portuguese Data Protection Authority (Comissão Nacional de Proteção de Dados, CNPD).
Data Retention Period
Personal data is kept only for as long as necessary for the purposes for which it was collected, or for as long as the law requires.
Where a newsletter has been subscribed to, the data is kept until that subscription is cancelled.
Changes to this Privacy Policy
Globalead Portugal reserves the right to amend this Privacy Policy whenever necessary.
Applicable Law
Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) and other applicable Portuguese legislation.
Contact
Email: geral@globalead.pt
